cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you saw me look at the door before the encore. Can you understand how it felt to keep expecting you?

mechanism: A coaches its pupil through acknowledging the personal cost of absence, correcting a factual excuse into recognition of waiting and hurt.
confusable: Not demanding explanation or repayment: A wants B to name what it felt like.
comparison: Concert missed despite intent versus long silence and insecurity.
seedUse: D75 train/concert/recording/door; S05 listening lesson and correction of superficial feeling label.
